name: MLWO World Heavyweight Championship
aka: MLWO Heavyweight Championship of the World
epitaph: The fed's top singles title. It was billed as the VPWF World Heavyweight Championship in the autumn of 1996, when Mauler carried it and Guy LaChance won it and lost it back. Marcus Renge and Jak Martin held it before Steve Sampson pinned Martin at Deadly Games on 22 March 1997; Martin won it back in a steel cage on 26 April, the first man to hold it twice. Marcus Renge won the five-man Torture Cage of Torture Chamber 2 on 26 October 1997, and Mister Robinson took it from Martin in the ladder match of Winter Inferno 97. Captain Midnight held it after February 1998 until it was handed to Steve Spector and dropped, leaving it vacant; Midnight won it back in a ladder match at May Madness 98 on 25 May 1998.

name: MLWO North American Championship
epitaph: The fed's second singles title. Angel of Pain lost it to Jim Mongol on the Wednesday Washout of 6 November 1996. Jak Martin, Sean Torrington and Danny Ice followed; Steve Sampson won it from Ice at Ground Zero on 28 June 1997, and the runner-up of the Torture Cage at Torture Chamber 2 took it under the match's own stipulation. Steve Spector won it from Matt Harris at Winter Inferno 97, and Tommy Marauder, the Man From Heck and Kevin Legend held it in 1998.

name: MLWO United States Championship
epitaph: The fed's third singles title. Joe Patrinne carried it in November 1996 and kept it against Venom on the Wednesday Washout of 6 November; Deathwatch was introduced as champion at Deadly Games on 22 March 1997. Mister Robinson defended it against Marcus Renge at Ground Zero on 28 June 1997, and Paradox won it from Jason Knight in a Texas Death Match at Torture Chamber 2 on 26 October 1997. Victor Vance and then Bishop held it in early 1998.

name: MLWO North American Tag Team Championship
aka: VPWF North American Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A tag team title that Da Ghetto Blasters lost to the Two Dudes With Attitude on the Wednesday Washout of 6 November 1996. ER, Michael Jeffries and Andrew Saunders, carried it in December 1996 and January 1997, and the fed's president announced in January 1997 that it would be unified with the world tag belts.

name: MLWO Unified Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The fed's tag title, billed as the World Tag Team Championship in 1996 and unified with the North American tag belts in 1997. The Mobb and Da Ghetto Blasters held it in the autumn of 1996 and the Rednecks and the Vegas Fighters in 1997; the Rednecks won it from the Vegas Fighters in a ladder match on May Madness: The Anniversary on 25 May 1997. The Good Knights defended it at Torture Chamber 2 on 26 October 1997 and lost it to the Rich and Infamous at Winter Inferno 97, whose retirement from the titles on the Saturday Slam of 28 March 1998 was a hoax. The Natural Born Annihilators, masked as Team LWC, won it in a three-way at May Madness 98 on 25 May 1998.

name: MLWO Lightweight Championship
epitaph: A singles title decided in a tournament that Matt Harris won over Sean Torrington, then billed Sean Stevens. Harris defended it against Steve Spector in a dog collar chain cage match on Slam Supercard 2 on 26 April 1997, and a 1998 introduction calls him the former and only MLWO Lightweight Champion.

name: MLWO Television Championship
epitaph: A title created in January 1998 from the former PCW Northwestern belt, with its first champion, Matt Harris, crowned in a torture cage match on the Saturday Slam of 24 January 1998. Vince Valor says Harris handed it to him, and Kevin Legend was later billed as the final MLWO Television champion.

name: MLWO HardCore Championship
epitaph: A weapons-match title carried in the autumn of 1996 by Marcus Renge, who is later introduced as the fed's longest reigning HardCore champion, and by Justin B in January 1997.

name: MLWO Mini World Championship
epitaph: A title for the fed's smaller wrestlers, which Jakito Martin kept against Mini-Dog on Battle Brawl II.
